channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Photobiomodulation therapy has a negligible effect as an adjunct to motor control exercise in people with chronic non-specific low back pain: a randomised trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=148) found that adding photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) to motor control exercise (MCE) had a negligible effect on pain intensity (MD -0.4 points, 95% CI -1.2 to 0.4), disability (MD -0.7 points, 95% CI -2.4 to 0.9), or circulating PGE2 concentrations compared with sham PBMT plus MCE in adults with chronic non-specific low back pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation (NMES) on Lower Limb Mobility and Activities of Daily Living in Post-Stroke Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 RCTs (579 patients) found that neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) significantly improved Fugl-Meyer Assessment (MD=3.40, P=0.001), ankle dorsiflexion ROM (MD=1.56, P=0.04), TUG (MD=-1.96, P=0.03), BBS (MD=10.78, P=0.005), PASS (MD=5.05, P<0.00001), and MBI (MD=13.29, P=0.02) in post-stroke patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy on pain intensity and functional disability in chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 RCTs found that extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT), particularly radial ESWT (rESWT), significantly reduced pain in chronic low back pain (SMD = -0.72; 95% CI -1.30 to -0.14), but functional disability improvements (MD = -6.12) did not reach the minimal clinically important difference.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical activity guidelines' impact on cognition in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 RCTs (n=462) found that meeting physical activity guidelines for multiple sclerosis (PAG-MS) significantly improved processing speed (SMD = 0.29), visuospatial memory (SMD = 0.47), and verbal memory (SMD = 0.75) in individuals with MS.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of treadmill exercise with and without vertical traction on gait, pain, disability, trunk proprioception, and depression in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain: A randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial with 45 chronic low back pain patients found that treadmill exercise with vertical traction and partial body weight support (VT+TE) led to greater improvements in Timed Up and Go performance, self-selected gait speed, disability, and trunk repositioning errors compared to treadmill exercise alone or core stabilization exercises.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Factors Associated With Response in Older Adults With Massive Irreparable Rotator Cuff Tears: A Four-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A 4-year prospective cohort study of 92 older adults with atraumatic massive irreparable rotator cuff tears found that 95-97% of patients achieved minimal clinically important difference at 3 months, with 100% achieving it by 4 years with nonoperative treatment. Longer symptom duration and smoking were associated with worse shoulder function, while diabetes was linked to higher pain intensity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Sensory Electrical Stimulation Versus Alternating Electromyography-Guided Electrical Stimulation on Functional Recovery of the Hand in Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A three-arm randomized controlled trial of 60 chronic stroke patients found that both Sensory Electrical Stimulation (SES) and alternating electromyography-guided electrical stimulation (Alt-EMG), combined with conventional physical therapy, produced greater improvements in Action Research Arm Test scores (adjusted mean gains of 12.05 and 12.44 points, respectively, both P < .001) compared to conventional physical therapy alone, with no significant difference between SES and Alt-EMG.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of short-foot and toe-curl exercises on movement control during single-leg landing after ACL reconstruction: An exploratory randomized controlled trial.
item.description: In ACLR patients, short-foot exercise (SFE) significantly reduced hip adduction excursion during single-leg landing compared to toe-curl exercise (TCE) at 6 weeks (between-group difference -6.30°, ES -1.41) and 12 weeks, suggesting SFE facilitates earlier improvement in frontal-plane movement control.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Measurement properties of observational gait analysis tools in neurological disorders: a COSMIN meta-analysis.
item.description: A COSMIN systematic review and meta-analysis of 28 articles found no observational gait analysis tool was fully recommended for use in neurological populations, but the Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS) and Gait Assessment and Intervention Tool (G.A.I.T.) showed the best potential for recommendation in stroke.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of Exercise Training on the Metabolic Cost of Walking in Health and Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 27 studies (N=1177) found chronic physical exercise training improved the metabolic cost of walking (g = 0.40, p = 0.001) in healthy adults (g = 0.49, p = 0.001), but not significantly in stroke patients (g = 0.24, p = 0.065).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Modality-specific, deficit-targeted exercise prescriptions for physical function in sarcopenia and frailty: a network meta-analysis
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 61 RCTs (N=3706) found multicomponent training with resistance training provided the most comprehensive benefits for functional mobility, while elastic band resistance training was most effective for handgrip strength (MD = 1.95 kg, 95% CI: 1.13 to 2.76) with moderate certainty.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Construct validity and intrasession intra-rater reliability of the stair and step tests in individuals with multiple sclerosis.
item.description: In 100 MS patients, both the Stair Test (ICC 0.997) and Step Test (ICC 0.955) showed excellent test-retest reliability and strong construct validity with other mobility scales. These tests offer a practical, fast, and low-fatigue solution for monitoring mobility in MS.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Trajectories of physical activity following digital education and exercise therapy-a longitudinal registry study among 15,197 persons with knee or hip osteoarthritis.
item.description: A longitudinal registry study of 15,197 individuals with knee or hip OA found that recommended physical activity levels rose from 51.4% at enrollment to 58.5% at one year following a digital education and exercise therapy program. Four distinct PA trajectories were identified, with BMI and physical function being key associated factors. All PA trajectories experienced clinically comparable improvements in patient-reported outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Balance confidence, balance, and gait capacity in chronic stroke: baseline and change correlations.
item.description: A secondary analysis of 168 independently ambulant adults with chronic stroke found small, non-significant correlations between Activities-specific Balance Confidence (ABC) scores and objective balance and gait measures at baseline and over time, supporting their assessment as complementary outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Investigating the Feasibility of Locomotor Training for Children Under 5 Years With Complex Neurodisabilties.
item.description: A single-group pre-post study of 71 children (mean age = 2.8 years) with neurodisabilities found a 6-week locomotor training program feasible and beneficial, with Goal Attainment Scaling scores increasing from 12.8 to 56.2 (85% achieving goals) and mobility outcomes exceeding clinically meaningful thresholds.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Technical and clinical feasibility of a pulmonary telerehabilitation model for people with COPD.
item.description: A two-phase feasibility study found that connected devices accurately monitored patients (≥99% clinical agreement) during pulmonary telerehabilitation, and an 8-week home-based program was feasible with high patient satisfaction and usability. Endurance time increased by a median of 171 seconds (95% CI 17-725).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of Wobble Board and Swiss Ball exercises on balance, mobility and functional independence in patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy
item.description: A study with 200 DPN patients (45-70 years) found both Wobble Board and Swiss Ball exercises, combined with conventional therapy, significantly improved Berg Balance Scale, Timed Up and Go, and Functional Independence Measure scores (all p < 0.001) after 8 weeks. The Swiss Ball group demonstrated statistically greater improvements across all outcomes.
item.author: Bull Fac Phys Ther

item.title: Low balance confidence in relation to strength training, walking, sitting, and physical function among women aged 75–105 years: a cross-sectional study within the Women’s Health Initiative Strong and Healthy (WHISH) Intervention Cohort
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 8,916 women aged 75–105 years in the WHISH cohort found that strength training ≥2 h/week (PR=0.76, 95% CI: 0.71–0.81) and walking ≥4.25 h/week (PR=0.41, 95% CI: 0.37–0.45) were associated with a lower prevalence of low balance confidence (<67% on ABC Scale). Conversely, sitting ≥8 h/day was associated with a higher prevalence (PR=1.24, 95% CI: 1.17–1.32).
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Divergent functional responses to hyperoxic versus hypoxic high-intensity interval training: a randomized exploratory active-comparator study
item.description: An exploratory randomized study with 23 active men found divergent functional responses to hyperoxic (FiO₂=0.60, n=13) versus hypoxic (FiO₂=0.16, n=10) Tabata-format HIIT over 3 weeks. Hyperoxia was associated with larger baseline-adjusted improvements in V̇O₂max (from 37.77 to 41.46 mL·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹) and ventilatory thresholds, and lower post-exercise peak lactate, compared to hypoxia.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Delivering a high-dose walking booster program after stroke: a multimethod study of therapists' beliefs and experiences nested within a randomized trial.
item.description: A multimethod study explored therapists' beliefs and experiences delivering a high-dose walking booster program (HiWalk) within a Phase II trial (n=6 therapists). Therapists believed high-dose training was important (98.5/100) but were less confident about patients completing 3 hours/day (74.8/100). Training, team support, and resources facilitated delivery, while beliefs about patient capability and resource limitations were barriers.
item.author: PubMed
